clue.text: To want a snake to appear inside is stingingly spiteful!

indicators.note: the snake is told to appear inside the verb for wanting, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to want is to wish
an asp is a small venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a snake to show up is being venomously nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp stings, so the adjective describes sharp, irritable malice.

clue.text: Another kind of winged duck

parts.note: a cryptic description: one more species of wild duck, its name also having another spelling without the D

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a freshwater dabbling duck, also spelt wigeon, the 'another kind' of spelling.

clue.text: Return to acting

parts.note: read as making a comeback in general, or literally going back to the theatre boards

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means making a successful return after time away, and the theatrical stage makes it literal for an actor.

clue.text: One old revolutionary god

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns things, so the letters of the next word are churned up

explanation.surface: An ancient revolutionary leader is revered like a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: An image worshipped as a deity, a false god.

clue.text: Bar renovated in time to give shelter

indicators.note: the rebuilt letters go in the time word, inside it

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: a renovated bar has been done over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub refurbished in good time so it can welcome customers in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' turns BAR into ARB, which 'in' puts inside HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to shelter or protect them.

clue.text: Room for most of the orchestra

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the ...é is a famous orchestra based in Manchester

explanation.surface: Asking for space for the bulk of the players.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a celebrated Manchester orchestra; drop its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A large room for meetings or concerts.

clue.text: Workman to pocket a female accessory

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to bag something is to take it, pocket it

explanation.surface: A labourer is about to steal a woman's accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag carried by women for purse, keys and the like.

clue.text: Mostly a machine for turning a narrow strip of wood

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the machine's name is used

parts.note: a lathe spins wood or metal to shape it

explanation.surface: A woodworking machine turns out thin strips.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin strip of wood, as used under plaster.

clue.text: Clergyman both before and after the due time

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: A churchman who is both early and tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking churchman such as a bishop.

clue.text: Top of the bill, the principal reason for going to the seaside?

definitions.text: the principal reason for going to the seaside?

explanation.definitionFit: The star act is the chief draw; read as main (the sea) attraction, the pull of the ocean draws people to the coast.

clue.text: Sell well at the zoo?

parts.note: an idiom for brisk business, pictured with roaring lions at a zoo

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have brisk business; the zoo picture adds literal roaring animals.

clue.text: Quits the flat

explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means owing nothing either way, level; a flat surface is level and smooth.

clue.text: Pastime becomes obsessive when horse involved

definitions.text: Pastime becomes obsessive when horse involved

parts.words: Pastime becomes obsessive when horse involved
parts.note: a pastime word that, joined to horse, makes the term for an obsession

explanation.definitionFit: A pastime done for pleasure; add horse and it becomes a pet obsession.

clue.text: South American once found in Callao

indicators.note: the person is found in the run of letters, sitting within the words

explanation.surface: An ancient South American turns up in the Peruvian port of Callao.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' points to the letters spanning 'in Callao'; Callao is a port in Peru, fitting the Inca surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire in the Andes before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: The Spanish in the Foreign Office name the criminal

indicators.note: the Spanish article goes in the abbreviation, within it

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spaniard inside the British Foreign Office identifies a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office is the British government department for foreign affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: Note could be going either way

indicators.note: the word reads the same backwards and forwards, so it goes either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A musical note could go in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A half note in music, worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Can rule out a type of energy

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Can a regulation exclude one form of power?
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is power from atomic fission or fusion.

clue.text: Let rigs be reconstructed with tough flexible tissue

indicators.note: to be reconstructed is to be rebuilt, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Oil rigs being rebuilt with tough material.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage, the chewy flexible tissue in meat.

clue.text: Thomas, a cricketer, say, has a game

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas

indicators.note: say signals that the cricketer is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball

explanation.surface: Thomas, who plays cricket, has a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BOWLER sounds like BOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle-style game of chance where tickets are drawn from a drum.

clue.text: Go dull like a mountain lake?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: Does a still mountain lake lose its shine?
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to lose lustre, as silver does.

clue.text: Free to a great extent it would seem

definitions.text: to a great extent it would seem

explanation.definitionFit: An escaped prisoner is free and roaming; read literally as 'at large' the words suggest great size.

clue.text: Hurried away on hearing a rumour

indicators.note: on hearing signals the rumour word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: word means news or rumour, as in 'word has it'

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off after catching some gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent WORD sounds the same as WHIRRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirred means moved quickly with a buzzing sound, as a machine rushing off.

clue.text: Wild African pig developed a growth

definitions.text: Wild African pig developed a growth

parts.words: Wild African pig developed a growth
parts.note: the animal's name is a hog with a growth on it, a swelling on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: A wild African swine named for the warty lumps on its face.

clue.text: Went down in the water the doctor admitted

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
to own up is to admit, so owned means admitted

explanation.surface: The doctor confessed someone sank.
explanation.definitionFit: To die or sink under water by suffocation.

clue.text: King has order for a garment

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: The monarch issues a command about clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose gown.

clue.text: Right after the drink comes a warning of danger

indicators.note: after puts the right abbreviation behind the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Correct drinking comes before a danger signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal warning of danger, as in an air-raid alarm.

clue.text: Repetition of sound from a screech-owl

indicators.note: from tells you to take the letters out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An owl's screech is heard again.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound heard again.

clue.text: Member in the team of warriors

annotationWithheld.why: 'Member in the team of warriors' as held: IMPI needs MP inside II, but no clue word gives the two I's
annotationWithheld.clue: Member in the team of warriors

clue.text: Stake for mountain climbing?

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the mountain's letters upwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily

explanation.surface: A post for a mountaineer?
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player's stake put in before the deal.

clue.text: Lack of understanding in a school exercise

parts.note: a comprehension is a reading test set in school

explanation.surface: Confusion in a class reading test.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to grasp the meaning, failing to understand.

clue.text: A bad habit that is hard to get out of

definitions.text: that is hard to get out of

explanation.definitionFit: A wicked habit; also a workshop clamp whose grip is hard to escape.

clue.text: Gammy leg Dane twisted having worked in the cornfield

indicators.note: a gammy leg is lame and crooked, which signals rearranging
twisted letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: A Dane with a bad leg wrenched it gathering in the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain after reapers.
